affected_system: food access, environmental health inspection, and community protection
alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on food-access and environmental-health service gaps
combine targeted inspection, monitoring, and data-quality repair for food-access and environmental-health service gaps
pair retail-access, inspection, price, and service triangulation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Food outlets, inspections, assistance, prices, access, and environmental complaints have separate semantics.
Area food access is not treated as individual diet, food security, or health outcome.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for food-access and environmental-health service gaps.

constraints.description: The food access and environmental health diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: environmental health commissioner and food-access program director
decision_question: Where do outlet access, affordability, verified hazards, inspection coverage, and assistance gaps coincide?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The food access and environmental health diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for food-access and environmental-health service gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: retail-access, inspection, price, and service triangulation

intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting food-access and environmental-health service gaps, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in people in high-need low-service conditions
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not convert request labels, outlet distance, or program nonparticipation into verified hazard or hunger.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for food-access and environmental-health service gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

title: Diagnose food-access and environmental-health service gaps
transportability_risks: Retail markets, informal food systems, inspection law, mobility, prices, and eligibility vary.
Administrative participation can understate eligible need.
